chapters.title: Already on a ship
pages: This ship is your home. Food is in your inventory. Furnace fuel goes in the generator and feeds both power and engines. Open the Ship Controller to choose where to go. Keep some supplies for getting back.
Choose a planet, landing pad or docking port, then press Jump. You can walk around while travelling. The countdown shows how long is left. A signal may offer food, fuel or salvage.

To explore a signal, press Investigate signal. Choose its docking port, then Dock. Open the normal door and walk through. Bring supplies back, Undock, then Resume journey. Your paid trip keeps its progress.

Search by room: food in the galley, fuel beside engineering, tools and parts at workbenches, building materials in cargo. Scouts share small spaces. Larger ships have separate rooms. Supplies do not refill when you come back.

chapters.title: Build my first ship
pages: Make a dirt or grass pad inside a cobblestone ring. Put a Pad Computer on the ring and click Register pad. You can keep its suggested name. Show pad area marks the ground that stays behind.

Above the pad, build a sealed hull with a normal door, Ship Controller, outward-facing engine, generator and inward-facing Air Supply. Leave standing room at the controller and clear space behind the engine.

Load furnace fuel in the generator. Close the door and open the Ship Controller. Launch checks the ship before leaving. Read any problem, repair it and try again. Home stays selected: use Land to return. Check ship is optional.

chapters.title: Landing pads
pages: Use a flat grass/dirt rectangle inside a complete cobblestone ring. Grass may become dirt. The interior and ship fit within 32 x 32 x 32.

Place the Pad Computer on the ring. Facing does not matter. Click Register pad with the suggested name, or edit it first. Show pad area and Show ship area highlight different parts; outlines fade after 30 seconds.
Leave clear sky above the ship. A stacked pad overhead obstructs launch. On landing, choose a pad on your current planet. Inspect again after repairs.

chapters.title: Hull and cargo
pages: Use full blocks for the pressure hull, full glass for windows and framed doors or trapdoors. Stairs, slabs and panes are fittings, not pressure seals.
Keep all ship parts connected. Pad dirt stays behind. Furnaces, storage and many workshop blocks travel with saved contents. Read Inspect for exact exceptions.
Stop moving pistons and pending actions before travel. Live explosives and world-bound machinery can block launch. Diagnostics name the broken block or machine.

chapters.title: Controllers
pages: One Ship Controller combines flight, travel, docking and engineering. Planets, landing pads and ports share one Destination selection. Launch, Jump, Land and Dock remain separate direct actions.
Computer Base is a crafting chassis; Computer Terminal runs NullOS. Machinery opens native controls and slots, with detailed terminals under Advanced.

chapters.title: Ship power
pages: Load any furnace fuel into a generator. Connected engines and generation share its real fuel slots. Top/side hoppers insert fuel; bottom hoppers remove empty containers. No cables or fuel pipes are needed.

Generation supplies demand and charges batteries; batteries cover shortages. Disabling generation leaves its fuel accessible to engines. Fuel burns only for real work, including stationary electrical use.

Engine, Generator, Battery and Scanner each accept the same System Upgrade item. Three slots give Stock, I, II and III. Battery modules cannot be removed until stored charge fits the smaller capacity.

chapters.title: Spatial air
pages: Air occupies a 32-cube grid. Pumps fill their outlet cells, then gas spreads through rooms. Breaches drain stored air. Crew uses air locally.
Air particles show filling, equalization and leaks. Full sealed rooms become quiet. Real vacuum leaks stay visible. Turning particles off does not stop oxygen use.
Keep the air-supply outlet inside the cabin and unobstructed. Watch room readings. Closing a door helps only if its frame and surrounding hull also seal.

chapters.title: Doors and groups
pages: The Ship Controller handles framed doors and trapdoors. Advanced engineering retains door groups and batch commands.
For docking place any standard door above one outward-facing Docking Base. Frame it, leave walking space inside and a clear approach outside. Iron doors work without extra buttons.

chapters.title: Suits and EVA
pages: Wear all four suit pieces. A sealed breathable cabin refills your oxygen. A suit has no separate crafted oxygen tank yet; keep a working ship air source.
In space, leaving the cabin enables flight. The tether limit is 72 blocks. Watch oxygen and return before it runs out. Airless planet surfaces retain normal gravity.
Airless ground drains oxygen away from a safe cabin/source. Wearing armor alone is not unlimited life support. Repair the cabin and monitor air before exploring.

chapters.title: Launch and land
pages: At the controller: Inspect hull, fix errors, close doors, then Launch. Blocks and cargo transfer to space with a loading screen. The hull stays stationary Minecraft blocks.
Recall EVA crew before travel. Landing restores the real hull at a clear registered pad. Do not quit during a loading screen. On reconnect, follow recovery messages.

chapters.title: Piloting
pages: Controller > Pilot. W/S thrust, A/D yaw, Space/Ctrl lift. Up/Down pitch, Q/E roll. R brakes; F fires the cannon. Only one crew member pilots.
Drag to orbit and use the wheel to zoom. H shows controls. Esc returns to the Ship Controller and stops motion. Ship camera is an observer view; it grants no thrust.
Power loss or unsafe crew stops flight. Local piloting stays in this region. Select a Destination and use Jump to change regions. Avoid solid bodies and other hulls.

chapters.title: Planet travel
pages: Choose one Destination: a region, landing pad or docking port. Jump takes time aboard the ship and keeps the final destination. Arrival is automatic; Land or Dock finishes the trip.
Terra is the overworld. Pelagos has grass and breathable air. Luna, Ares and Cinder are airless. New surfaces are flat; first arrival creates a starter pad.
Launching returns to that planet orbit. Existing overworld pads belong to Terra. Jump back to Sol/Terra before landing at home.

chapters.title: Scanners
pages: One Scanner lists nearby destinations. Select a result and Set destination; the controller uses that same selection. Looking at a target never starts travel.
Install System Upgrades: Stock range 1024, then 2048/4096/8192. The first module enables distant destinations. Cameras and scanners need Cameras power; Advanced holds allocation tuning.

chapters.title: Cameras
pages: Mount a small Camera on a solid wall, pointing toward the view. Right-click to name it, see a live preview, enable it or view fullscreen. Esc returns from fullscreen to setup.
Mount thin Monitor blocks like pictures. Complete rectangles up to 8 x 8 share one named camera feed. Right-click any tile to select a camera for the wall. Old cube displays keep their hull seals.
A fullscreen feed uses arrows to aim, Page Up/Down to zoom and F2 to capture. Tab changes eligible feeds. Ground feeds cover a bounded neighborhood.
Camera loading does not tick distant machines or TNT. A feed fills in as terrain arrives. Unsupported renderer details may differ from a normal player view.

chapters.title: NullOS terminal
pages: Computer Terminal opens an 80-column console. It keeps files and jobs with the ship. It uses a custom runtime isolated from host files, processes and networks.
Keep Controls powered for ship calls. Up/Down recalls commands. Ctrl-C stops a foreground job; Shift-Esc closes the console. A standalone terminal can still edit files.

chapters.title: Shell commands
pages:
Try these commands:
help
ls
ship status
ship rooms
python air.py
bash seal.sh

seal.sh closes doors.
Files: pwd, cd, ls, cat, echo, mkdir, cp, mv, rm. Pipes support grep, head, wc. Use > to replace a file and >> to append. These paths stay inside the guest disk.
edit name.py starts a replacement editor. Type lines. A single . line or Ctrl-S saves; Ctrl-C cancels. cat name.py reads it back.

chapters.title: Scripts and jobs
pages:
Bash-style: bash file.sh
Python-style:
python file.py

Loops, branches and native ship functions are supported. These are language subsets, not full Bash/Python.
run --detach file.py leaves a job running. ps lists jobs; kill ID stops one. Foreground jobs pause without a viewer. Files and detached jobs survive a restart.
Detached jobs compute while chunks unload. World actions wait for the full hull to load again. Jobs use the last known power state while unloaded.

chapters.title: Native ship API
pages:
Shell: ship rooms
Python:
print(ship.rooms())

Other calls handle power, doors, devices, scanners, cameras, firing and bounded flight.

Try: ship scan local
ship scan long
ship doors all close

The usual power and safety checks apply. Travel scripts need online crew near the Ship Controller.

chapters.title: Damage and cannon
pages: The cannon needs connected, enabled hardware and Weapons power. Press F while piloting to fire. Normal recharge rules apply.
Damage removes real hull and equipment. Breaches lose air; severed hardware loses the bus. Repair survivors before travel. Material blast resistance still matters.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
pages: Pad not found? Put its computer on the cobble ring at floor height. Fill the interior with grass/dirt. Repair border holes and check for overlapping ownership.
No power? Load generator fuel; check battery, enabled switches, connected hull and allocations. No scanner feed? Add one Cameras slot per enabled camera/scanner.
Losing air? Check room readings, exterior doors, hatch frames and breaches. Engine blocked? Clear its outward exhaust. Inspect names unsupported machines and travel obstacles.
Cannot land? Jump to the right planet, choose a registered pad and clear its volume. Crew or cargo not ready? Recall crew and wait for the loading handshake.

chapters.title: Crafting notes
pages: Recipes follow in this book: real items in a 3 x 3 grid; hover for names, click a crafted part for its recipe. Mirroring works, rotation does not. Circuit boards craft in fours; wooden doors accept any wood.

chapters.title: Ship beacons
pages: Place a Ship Beacon on a registered pad ring. Its catalog shows designs, a footprint and readiness. Select a model, then Deliver ship. Delivery is free; stand clear of the pad.
New ships include fuel, a Ship Controller and a compact door-on-base port. Enter normally, close the door, inspect and launch. Existing builds and their fuel are preserved.
Clear the pad and sky. Resume interrupted delivery with the same design. Operators can visit six examples with /nullspace shipyard.

chapters.title: Star systems
pages: Each world has its own galaxy: Sol and four random systems, plus nebulae, asteroid fields and stranger places. The Scanner's Stars page is the map: green is one jump away, grey needs hops.

Jumps cost 1.00 fuel plus 0.10 per light-year. Engine upgrades set range: 25, 40, 60 or 100 ly. Tier 2 needs an Advanced Upgrade (amethyst), tier 3 an Exotic one (netherite scrap or echo shards). Further out is more dangerous and richer.

chapters.title: Stations and docks
pages: Space regions automatically contain stations. At the controller choose Destination > Ports, select a station berth, then Dock. Autopilot handles approach and mating. Scanners share the same ship destination.
After capture, open the normal dock door and walk through. A short transition boards the other vessel. Return through the same port, then Undock. Crew must be aboard breathable cabins.

Carry a Station Core, suit and module kits. Deploy station from the controller, open the dock door and walk through wearing the suit. The core shows room tiles, Build buttons and separate access fields.
